s: If this type comes, solve like this

s.q: If an equation contains both $z$ and $\bar z$ (or $|z|$) and asks for the solutions or $\sum|z|^2$
s.s: Put $z=x+iy$ in the equation. || Separate real and imaginary parts and set each side equal: two real equations in $x,y$. || Solve the two equations (often one factorises, e.g. $y(2x+1)=0$). || Compute what is asked ($|z|^2$, sum of solutions…). || Shortcut: when $|z|$ appears with $z$, the imaginary part fixes $y$ immediately.
s.e: $|z|+z=3+i$: imaginary part gives $y=1$; real part $\sqrt{x^2+1}+x=3\Rightarrow x^2+1=(3-x)^2\Rightarrow x=\frac43$, so $|z|=\frac53$.

s.q: If high powers of $\omega$, $i$, $1\pm i$, $-1\pm i\sqrt3$ or $\frac{1+i}{1-i}$ appear
s.s: Recognise the building blocks: $-1+i\sqrt3=2\omega$, $-1-i\sqrt3=2\omega^2$, $1\pm i=\sqrt2e^{\pm i\pi/4}$. || Write each number in polar form $re^{i\theta}$. || Apply De Moivre: $(re^{i\theta})^n=r^ne^{in\theta}$. || Reduce the angle modulo $2\pi$ (or the power of $\omega$ modulo 3, of $i$ modulo 4). || Simplify using $1+\omega+\omega^2=0$.

s.q: If a locus is described and you must identify it (line, circle, arc) or use it
s.r: Conditions such as $|z-a|=|z-b|$, $\left|\frac{z-a}{z-b}\right|=k$, $\arg\frac{z-a}{z-b}=\theta$, $\operatorname{Re}\frac{z-a}{z-b}=0$, or $\frac{z-i}{z+i}$ purely real.
s.s: First try to recognise the standard locus from the shape of the condition. || If unsure, put $z=x+iy$ and simplify to a Cartesian equation. || For a circle, read centre and radius; for an arc, the chord $ab$ subtends angle $\theta$. || Then answer the question (intersection with another curve, a distance, a value).
s.e: $\operatorname{Re}\frac{z-1}{z+1}=0$ ⇒ $\angle$ at $z$ is $90^\circ$ ⇒ circle with diameter from $-1$ to $1$: $|z|=1$ (excluding $z=-1$).

s.q: If it asks the maximum or minimum of $|z-z_1|$ (or $|az+b|$) when $z$ lies on a circle or in a region
s.f: z\ \text{on circle centre } c,\ \text{radius } r:\ \ |z-z_1|_{\min/\max}=\big||z_1-c|\mp r\big|
s.s: Turn the expression into a distance: $|3iz+6|=3|z-2i|$ = $3\times$ distance from $2i$. || Find the centre $c$ and radius $r$ of the region. || Distance from the point to the centre is $d=|z_1-c|$. || Maximum $=d+r$; minimum $=|d-r|$ (or $0$ if the point lies inside a disc). || The extreme point lies on the line through $c$ and $z_1$.
s.e: $|z-3|=2$; max $|z+1|$ = distance from $-1$ to $3$ plus radius $=4+2=6$.

s.q: If it asks the area of a region in the Argand plane defined by several conditions
s.s: Convert every condition to $x,y$ (discs, half-planes). || Sketch them and shade the intersection. || Compute the area with sectors and triangles.

s.q: If a real polynomial has a complex root, or complex roots with a condition
s.r: "$\alpha=1$, $\beta=1+i\sqrt2$ are roots of $x^3+ax^2+bx+c$", or roots of $x^2+\sqrt6x+3=0$ raised to powers.
s.f: \text{real coefficients}\Rightarrow\text{complex roots come in conjugate pairs}
s.s: Add the conjugate of every given complex root to the list of roots. || Use Vieta (sum, sum of products, product) to get the coefficients. || For powers of roots, write roots in polar form and use De Moivre.

s.q: If it is geometry with rotation: square, equilateral triangle, right angle at a point
s.r: "rotate $z_1$ through a right angle", "$OAB$ is an equilateral triangle", "vertices of a square".
s.s: To rotate $z$ about $z_0$ by $\theta$ (anticlockwise): $z'-z_0=(z-z_0)e^{i\theta}$; by $90^\circ$ multiply by $i$. || For a triangle condition, write the rotation from one side to another. || Solve for the unknown vertex, then answer.

s.q: If a complex fraction must be purely real or purely imaginary
s.s: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator. || The denominator becomes real; look at the numerator. || Set its imaginary part (for "real") or real part (for "imaginary") to zero. || Solve the resulting trig/algebraic equation.

s.q: If it uses modulus/argument rules of products and quotients
s.s: Replace moduli of products by products of moduli. || Convert argument conditions to $z=re^{i\theta}$ forms. || Simplify and compute.
